hunks.baseline: Tiny fragments of stone trembled. So did the countless corpses, eyes wide open in death.
hunks.sol: Tiny fragments of stone trembled. So did the countless corpses, their eyes wide open in death.

hunks.baseline: This tremor was undeniable proof that at least several thousand men and horses were closing in on them.
hunks.sol: This tremor was undeniable proof that at least several thousand men and horses were closing in.

hunks.baseline: The cruel omen was enough to give some people hope, and others utter despair.
hunks.sol: The cruel omen was enough to give some people hope, and others deep despair.

hunks.baseline: “Khan Jamukha has arrived!”
hunks.sol: “Jamukha Khan has arrived!”

hunks.baseline: A name unfamiliar even to the people of Shanxi. The ruler of the western grasslands, the undisputed master of the vast Great Steppe. And now, at least several thousand reinforcements had joined him.
hunks.sol: A name unfamiliar to the people of Shanxi. The ruler of the western grasslands, the absolute master of the vast Great Steppe. As if his arrival weren’t enough, at least several thousand reinforcements had joined him.

hunks.baseline: The nomads’ morale, which had been sinking as steadily as a dying ember while they were pushed back, soared. The Shanxi defenders, who had been driving back the invaders moments ago, felt the fatigue and fear they had forgotten return to them.
hunks.sol: The nomads had been pushed back, their morale dwindling like a dying ember. Now it soared. The Shanxi defenders, who had been driving back the invaders moments ago, felt their forgotten fatigue and fear return.

hunks.baseline: As if to prove how fierce the battle had been, blood from his enemies ran down his sword, the weapon of the commander in chief.
hunks.sol: Blood from his enemies ran down the commander in chief’s sword, proof of how fiercely he had fought.

hunks.baseline: He had fought with everything he had.
hunks.sol: He had given the battle everything he had.

hunks.baseline: He had joined the fighting himself to raise his men’s spirits. Whenever a crisis arose, he had given flawless orders, sealing the gorge entrance so thoroughly that not even a drop of water could pass.
hunks.sol: He had joined the fighting himself to raise his men’s spirits. Whenever a crisis arose, his orders had sealed the gorge entrance tight.

hunks.baseline: Less than half of those fifteen thousand could be called the main force, and even they had suffered heavy losses fighting the enemies who kept pouring in.
hunks.sol: Less than half of those fifteen thousand could be called the main force, and even they had suffered heavy losses against the enemies who kept pouring in.

hunks.baseline: In this long, dreadful war of attrition around the narrow gorge, it was not the rocks that broke first, but the pebbles.
hunks.sol: In this long, dreadful war of attrition around the narrow gorge, it was not the rocks that would break first, but the pebbles.

hunks.baseline: Enemies and allies charged at one another over heaps of corpses, all tangled together. His retainer’s cries to him as he stood rooted to the spot were drowned out by the enemy’s shouts, reaching him only in broken snatches, like stepping-stones across a stream.
hunks.sol: Enemies and allies charged over heaps of corpses and tangled together. He stood rooted to the spot while a retainer called to him, but the enemy’s shouts drowned out the words. They reached him only in broken snatches, like stepping-stones across a stream.

hunks.baseline: A hand tugging hard at his sleeve.
hunks.sol: A hand tugged hard at his sleeve.

hunks.baseline: A face full of desperation and urgency.
hunks.sol: The retainer’s face was full of desperation and urgency.

hunks.baseline: And it wasn’t just the retainer in front of him. Everyone around him—the martial artists of the Jin Family of Taiyuan, the Sect Leaders of their vassal sects, and the government troops—was speaking to him with their eyes.
hunks.sol: And it wasn’t just the man in front of him. Everyone around him—the martial artists of the Jin Family of Taiyuan, the Sect Leaders of their vassal sects, and the government troops—was speaking to him with their eyes.

hunks.baseline: While the troops at the front held out to buy time, he—the commander in chief—could gather the remaining forces and withdraw. That was the best strategy.
hunks.sol: While the troops at the front fought to the death to buy time, he—the commander in chief—could gather the remaining forces and withdraw.

hunks.baseline: Jin Wikyung smiled faintly and closed his hand around the sword hilt he had been holding loosely.
hunks.sol: Jin Wikyung smiled faintly and tightened his grip on his sword hilt.

hunks.baseline: A Keshik trying to break through his guards crumpled without a fight.
hunks.sol: A Keshik who had broken through his guards crumpled without a fight.

hunks.baseline: Jin Wikyung advanced, cutting down the enemy with clean, precise movements. His retainer hurried after him again.
hunks.sol: Jin Wikyung advanced, cutting down the enemy with clean, precise movements. His retainer hurried after him.

hunks.baseline: “Tell Lee Seowol, the Sect Leader of the Mount Heng Sword Sect, that from this moment on, I entrust everything that follows to her.”
hunks.sol: “Tell Lee Seowol, the Sect Leader of the Mount Heng Sword Sect, that from this moment on, I’m leaving everything that follows to her.”

hunks.baseline: A defeated general had nowhere to return to. After sacrificing the lives of so many of his people, this was where he belonged.
hunks.sol: A defeated commander had nowhere to return to. After sacrificing the lives of so many of his people, this was where he belonged.

hunks.baseline: *I promised everyone. I would protect this land—Shanxi Province.*
hunks.sol: *I promised everyone I would protect this land—Shanxi Province.*

hunks.baseline: A shiver, its origin unknown, raced from the crown of their heads through their entire bodies.
hunks.sol: A shiver, its origin unknown, raced from the crowns of their heads through their bodies.

hunks.baseline: It was the pain of his flesh, which he had momentarily forgotten, and the vague helplessness of facing an insurmountable wall.
hunks.sol: It was the pain he had forgotten for a moment, and the helplessness of facing a wall too high to overcome.

hunks.baseline: Jin Mukyung looked up at the sky and muttered inwardly.
hunks.sol: Jin Mukyung looked up at the sky and asked himself the question.

hunks.baseline: “Speak with your sword, not that silver tongue of yours. A provocation like that doesn’t suit someone like you.”
hunks.sol: “Speak with your sword, not that tongue of yours. A provocation like that doesn’t suit someone like you.”

hunks.baseline: “You’re still far too clumsy. Though, of course, choosing the wrong opponent was a big part of it. Like that pathetic fool lying over there.”
hunks.sol: “You’re still far too clumsy at it. Though choosing the wrong opponent was a big part of it. Like that pathetic fool lying over there.”

hunks.baseline: For a moment, Jin Mukyung understood what he meant and let out a quiet laugh.
hunks.sol: Jin Mukyung understood what he meant and let out a quiet laugh.

hunks.baseline: “You want me to surrender? To you, of all people?”
hunks.sol: “You want me to surrender? Me, of all people?”

hunks.baseline: “No. I mean submit. Roll over and show your belly to your master, wag your tail, and lick his feet like a dog.”
hunks.sol: “No. I mean submit. Roll over and show your belly to your master, wag your tail, and lick the tops of his feet like a dog.”

hunks.baseline: Jin Mukyung slowly raised his sword upright and spoke through its white blade.
hunks.sol: Jin Mukyung slowly raised his sword upright and spoke across its white blade.

hunks.baseline: “I’ll spare your life. Yours, and all of theirs.”
hunks.sol: “I’ll spare you. You and all of them.”

hunks.baseline: A leash alone was not enough.
hunks.sol: A collar alone was not enough.

hunks.baseline: A hunting dog kept on a tight leash and starved for days on end would grow docile. It would have no strength left to bite anyone, and in the helplessness it had never experienced before, it would realize it was nothing but an animal.
hunks.sol: A hunting dog kept in a sturdy collar and starved for days on end would grow docile. It would have no strength left to bite anyone, and in the helplessness it had never experienced before, it would realize it was an animal.

hunks.baseline: Wrong.
hunks.sol: No.

hunks.baseline: That he could save the people continuing a blood-soaked battle whose ending was already decided, his one and only older brother, and the two Peak masters waiting to die behind him.
hunks.sol: That he could save the people fighting on in a blood-soaked battle whose ending was already decided, his one and only hyung, and the two Peak masters waiting to die behind him.

hunks.baseline: Jin Mukyung looked at the two men shouting with what little strength they had left, his gaze sunk deep.
hunks.sol: Jin Mukyung looked at the two men shouting with what little strength they had left, his gaze heavy.

hunks.baseline: Jin Mukyung looked at Jamukha and parted his lips.
hunks.sol: Jin Mukyung looked at Jamukha and spoke.

hunks.baseline: Jamukha’s smile had faded a little as Jin Mukyung stepped toward him.
hunks.sol: Jamukha’s smile faded a little as Jin Mukyung stepped toward him.

hunks.baseline: With a single phrase, spat out through clenched teeth, he answered:
hunks.sol: He spat out his answer through clenched teeth.

hunks.baseline: Far away, the resonance of dozens of horns reached the gorge at once.
hunks.sol: Far away, the sound of dozens of horns blowing at once reached the gorge.

hunks.baseline: The tremor everyone in the gorge had felt moments ago hadn’t belonged only to the nomads.
hunks.sol: The tremor everyone in the gorge had felt moments ago hadn’t come from the nomads alone.
